ndjson_policy.description: Machine NDJSON codes/Display stay English; suggestions follow locale.

preference_action.description: Present when `--set` / `--clear` mutated the preference file.

write_strategy.description:
Write strategy the atomic layer used for the preference file.

Present only when this run wrote or removed the preference, so a plain
report never claims a mechanism it did not use. `--clear` reports
`none`, because it unlinks the file instead of writing content.

backup_skipped.description: Why the requested backup was skipped, when the directory refused it.

ok.description: Outcome of the run, stamped by the writer

code.description: Machine error code, present when ok is false

exit.description: Process exit status, present when ok is false

target_resolved.description: Absolute targets the run resolved, in invocation order, and never a joined string, so a path holding `,` stays readable; a run with one target publishes a one-item array, so the shape never depends on the count

target_source.description: Where the target came from: named in the invocation line, inherited from the workspace slot, or the standard-input stream

workspace_source.description: Where the workspace root came from: the `--workspace` flag or the process working directory

records_suppressed.description: Records the writer dropped before the terminal event: `--filter` rejections, `--select` projections that emptied the record, dedupe duplicates and `--limit` cuts. It counts records, never files, so it does not compare with `files_matched`: one file can contribute several records

files_budget_dropped.description: Entries the `--limit` budget dropped, in the unit the verb produces: files for walking verbs, records for streaming ones; a floor, because workers may stop before producing the rest

files_planned.description: Files the run would have modified in `--dry-run` or `--preview`; absent from a run that really wrote

truncated.description: The record itself was cut by `--truncate-content` or `--max-output-bytes`, so the fields are shorter than the source

truncated_records.description: Records the writer cut this run, counted once per record
